components.published_behavior: Long autonomous executions and research artifacts
components.implementation: CLI, TUI and loopback web inspect resolved routing, experiments, literature, coding/audit histories and immutable artifact bytes; pause/resume and budget edits use the durable engine. CLI, TUI and web expose archived AI behavior, exact prompts, graph contracts, actual call provenance and generic subordinate accounting. Guided startup and shared private settings across CLI/TUI/web explain prerequisites, preserve partial setup and reject stale edits without changing existing runs. Metis branding and the metis CLI entry point establish independent project identity; autoresearch remains a compatibility alias. Managed OpenSSH connections discover configured aliases and accept new hosts, handle host trust/password/passphrase/MFA in the interfaces, provision a private runtime, and reconnect to detached remote controllers. Database storage can be selected separately from shared experiment files. The exact charcoal/cream/terracotta palette and concise host/scientist voice span browser, terminal and CLI. Question-led startup carries an inquiry into explicit setup. The TUI mirrors browser destinations with a wide sidebar or compact navigation, four research tabs, readable evidence summaries and scrollable complete receipts. Visible setup sections retain edits. Command search and concise terminal status preserve access to advanced inspection without changing research configuration or execution gates. Web project-first onboarding provides bounded read-only discovery, explicit separately budgeted AI setup proposals with exact outbound previews, saved failure/usage receipts, evidence-cited selected application, inert adapter drafts, plain command entry and a three-step review. Shared readiness guidance orders root prerequisites; the browser automatically performs read-only source inspection when project setup needs evidence, keeps full diagnostics available, and asks for original benchmark values, credentials and host changes. Malformed credential references are not echoed in writer readiness. No proposal executes code or silently changes research settings. Workspace settings begins with reusable model access and server-side credential guidance; New research leads with the question and source, derives an optional run name, and keeps manual and advanced setup available. Invalid variable-name input clears before browser help can echo it; readiness still does not contact a provider. Home includes a decorative three-dimensional temple assembled from individually falling stones, with local mouse/keyboard rotation, pause and replay. The unframed browser scene has a single corner replay icon and no ground grid; pause and reset remain keyboard actions. Browser voxel rendering and a simpler terminal Unicode outline share packaged timing and initial view; reduced motion shows the completed temple, offscreen scenes pause and construction stops after assembly. Animation carries no research-progress or scientific-capability claim. The browser keeps local/SSH status at bottom left and opens a compact, searchable top picker for saved profiles and configured aliases; existing authentication prompts and detailed installation remain explicit. Authenticated browser Check setup repairs bounded eligible source include lists, builds missing Docker images from simple pinned Python requirements in a minimal context or fetches the configured image, and rechecks readiness without creating a run. Model access exposes an unsaved Google routing profile, separate credential destinations and optional Laya service fields. CLI profile application updates future defaults only; credential mutations guard destination changes and narrow keyboard focus clears the sticky footer. Setup now selects bounded eligible project files without asking users for inclusion patterns, repairs partial selections hiding command scripts, and previews resolved filenames in Review. A dedicated browser Settings page exposes global, workspace and project model/Laya scopes, override/reset controls and preserved drafts. Shared CLI/TUI resolution keeps future-run defaults current while recorded runs remain fixed. Connected SSH controllers synchronize only model configuration and report pending failures. Browser inquiry setup now creates unique private project folders when the path is blank or explicitly requested, or selects existing directories through an authenticated host-side picker. Manual experiment commands and metrics are advanced protocol overrides; empty folders remain scientifically unready. Saved SSH profiles expose remote experiment-file storage in the primary connection form; readiness diagnostics show the resolved research and database directories separately.
components.remaining_gap: Implemented engineering extension, not a scientific capability claim. Target deployments must provision and validate their own API/runtime services. Remote deployments require a supported Python, site-approved controller lifetime, persistent SQLite-compatible database storage and remote provider credentials; live MFA depends on the host authentication policy. AI onboarding quality is unmeasured; suggested commands and adapter drafts need project-specific implementation and live verification. Custom GPU batch launchers remain outside the generic Slurm backend. The compact picker was inspected with synthetic hosts; this interface change was not exercised against a live SSH target. Automatic image construction covers only simple pinned Python requirements; dependency execution, project benchmark behavior and non-Python environments remain unverified. On Berzelius, project NFS can hold experiment artifacts but the login-node controller still lacks a documented persistent host-local database path; choosing project storage alone does not establish a durable connection.
